title: Pod Lifecycle
content: Pending includes time spent waiting for scheduling and for container image downloads. Container states are Waiting, Running, and Terminated; terminated state includes a reason and exit code.

title: Pod Lifecycle
section: How Pods handle problems with containers
content: CrashLoopBackOff indicates repeated container startup failures with restart backoff. Possible causes include application errors, configuration problems, resource constraints, and failed startup or liveness probes. Inspect logs and container status to distinguish them.

title: Deployments
content: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets during a rollout and retains revision history for rollback. A paused Deployment must be resumed before rollback; setting revisionHistoryLimit to zero removes rollback history after cleanup.

title: Service
content: A Service normally targets Pods selected by labels. The Service controller updates EndpointSlices for matching Pods. Service port and targetPort can differ; inspect the selector and backend port when traffic cannot reach Pods.

title: Debug Services
section: Does the Service have any EndpointSlices?
content: When a Service has no endpoints, compare its spec.selector with Pod metadata.labels. A selector typo can leave EndpointSlices without backends. Check whether selected Pods are working before attributing the failure to the Service.

title: EndpointSlices
content: EndpointSlices track backend network addresses for a Service. For a Service with a selector, the control plane creates EndpointSlices referencing Pods that match that selector.

title: Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes
content: A failing readiness probe removes a container from Service traffic without restarting it. A failed liveness probe can restart a container. A startup probe delays liveness and readiness probes until startup succeeds.

title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
content: An HTTP probe uses its configured path and port to check the container. Failed readiness checks keep the Pod unready; repeated startup or liveness failures can cause container restarts. Check probe response and failure events.

title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
content: The scheduler uses CPU and memory requests to decide placement. Memory limits are enforced at runtime, and a container exceeding its memory limit can be OOM killed. Pending Pods with FailedScheduling events may indicate insufficient requested resources.

title: ConfigMaps
section: Using ConfigMaps as files and environment variables
content: Pods can consume ConfigMap data through environment variables, command arguments, or mounted configuration files. A container may reference a specific ConfigMap key for an environment variable.

title: Define Environment Variables for a Container
content: Container environment variables can be defined with env for individual values or envFrom to load values from a ConfigMap or Secret. Inspect the Pod template when an application reports a missing environment variable.

title: DNS for Services and Pods
content: Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods. A Service name can be resolved within its namespace; cross namespace service discovery uses a qualified name. Check DNS and Service endpoints separately.

title: Images
content: ImagePullBackOff means Kubernetes could not pull a container image and is retrying with backoff. An invalid image name or missing credentials for a private registry are possible causes; inspect the waiting reason and events.

title: Assigning Pods to Nodes
content: The scheduler places Pods on nodes that satisfy resource capacity and placement constraints. nodeSelector and affinity can restrict eligible nodes. Inspect FailedScheduling events when a Pod remains Pending.

title: Persistent Volumes
content: A PersistentVolumeClaim requests storage capacity and access modes, and binds to a compatible PersistentVolume. A claim can remain Pending when no matching volume is available or a specified volume is already bound.

title: Debug Running Pods
content: Pod details show container state, readiness, restart count, and recent events. Current and previous container logs help investigate running or crashing Pods and distinguish possible failure causes.
